title: Chapter 9 Quiz
description: Test your deep knowledge of the MonoBehaviour lifecycle, execution order, and best practices!

questions.question: Which method is called first when a new GameObject is instantiated (with scripts attached)?
questions.explanation: Awake is called before OnEnable and Start.

questions.question: Is Awake() called if the script component is initially disabled?
options: Only if the GameObject is active
questions.explanation: Awake runs regardless of the component's enabled state.

questions.question: What is the best method to get a reference to a Rigidbody on the same GameObject?
questions.explanation: Awake is suitable for self-component retrieval because it's early and doesn't depend on others.

questions.question: Which method is called every time a GameObject is set from inactive to active?
questions.explanation: OnEnable fires each time the object becomes active.

questions.question: If you need to communicate with another object that was just instantiated, where should you do it?
questions.explanation: Start ensures that the other object's Awake has already run.

questions.question: How many times per frame can FixedUpdate be called?
questions.explanation: If the frame rate is high, FixedUpdate may run multiple times; if low, it may skip.

questions.question: What does Time.deltaTime return inside FixedUpdate?
questions.explanation: Inside FixedUpdate, Time.deltaTime is automatically replaced with the fixed timestep.

questions.question: Which method should you use to apply continuous force to a Rigidbody?
questions.explanation: Physics forces should be applied in FixedUpdate for stable simulation.

questions.question: Why is LateUpdate ideal for camera follow scripts?
options: It runs after all Update methods, ensuring the player has moved
It runs at a fixed timestep
questions.explanation: LateUpdate guarantees the target has finished its Update logic.

questions.question: When is OnDisable called?
options: Only when the object is destroyed
When the object becomes inactive or its script is disabled
questions.explanation: OnDisable handles deactivation and script disabling.

questions.question: What is a common use of OnDisable?
questions.explanation: To prevent memory leaks, unsubscribe from events in OnDisable.

questions.question: Which method is guaranteed to be called when the application quits?
questions.explanation: OnApplicationQuit is specifically designed for quit handling.

questions.question: OnDestroy is always called when a scene is unloaded.
questions.explanation: If the object has DontDestroyOnLoad, it won't be destroyed on scene unload.

questions.question: How can you guarantee that ScriptA's Awake runs before ScriptB's Awake?
options: Place ScriptA higher in the Hierarchy
questions.explanation: Script Execution Order in Project Settings allows you to define priority.

questions.question: What does a negative execution order number mean?
questions.explanation: Lower (more negative) numbers execute earlier.

questions.question: What is the attribute to set default execution order in code?
questions.explanation: [DefaultExecutionOrder(value)] sets the script's order.

questions.question: You move a player's Transform in Update, but the camera following in Update shows jitter. What's the likely fix?
questions.explanation: LateUpdate ensures the camera reads the player's position after it has moved.

questions.question: If you instantiate a prefab and want to access it in Start, can you assume its Awake has already run?
options: Yes, because Start runs after Awake
No, order is not guaranteed across objects
Only if the prefab is a child
questions.explanation: Start is called after all Awakes in the scene (including newly instantiated objects) have completed, so it's safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good use of OnEnable/OnDisable pair?
questions.explanation: Physics forces should be in FixedUpdate, not tied to enable state.

questions.question: You can rely on the default execution order being the same every time you play.
questions.explanation: Default order is not deterministic across scripts unless you set it.

questions.question: What is the best place to find a reference to another object that might not exist at scene start?
questions.explanation: If the object may spawn later, checking in Update (or using events) is safe.

questions.question: Which lifecycle method is called only once per script instance, even if the GameObject is re-enabled many times?
questions.explanation: Start and Awake run only once per instance; OnEnable repeats.

questions.question: If you have code in OnDisable that accesses other objects, what precaution should you take?
options: Check for null or use try-catch
questions.explanation: Other objects may already be destroyed; null checks prevent errors.

questions.question: Why is OnApplicationQuit preferred over OnDestroy for saving game data?
options: OnDestroy may not be called on quit in some situations
questions.explanation: OnDestroy is not guaranteed on application quit (especially on mobile/WebGL).
